Concede

/kuhn-SEED/ - rhymes with indeed · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Concede means to admit that a point is valid.

Halfway through the review, the architect conceded that the north stairwell was too narrow and sketched a wider one.

Worked Example

Two mapmakers had argued for a decade about the river's true source. When the survey photographs came back, the elder studied them for a long minute, then conceded — his rival's tributary ran higher.

Concede is the argument-word among this unit's yielders: you concede a point, an error, a game. It means admitting the other side has it right and giving up that ground, even while the larger contest goes on.

How Concede Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

admit

admit: to own that something is true — everyday, no contest implied

grant

grant: to allow a point for argument's sake, sometimes without believing it

Antonyms

deny

deny: to insist it is not so

contest

contest: to keep fighting the point

How Strong Is It? — acknowledge → concede → surrender

acknowledge vs. concede

acknowledge vs. concede: To acknowledge a point is only to show you heard it — you can acknowledge an objection and still give it nothing.

surrender vs. concede

surrender vs. concede: Surrender goes further than concede — conceding yields one point and plays on; surrendering hands over the whole contest.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: wholly, together

Root — ced-

Root — ced-: to go, to yield

Put it together

Put it together: Con- (wholly) + ced- (to go, yield) = to yield entirely. Latin concedere was to give way, to grant. English narrowed it to the argument: when you concede, you stop defending one piece of ground and let the other side take it. The same ced- travels through this unit's accede and through the bare verb cede itself.

Use the root in a new word: cede

Use the root in a new word: cede: Under the 1867 agreement the islands were ceded to the mainland government.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / argumentative

Concede lives in debates, games, and negotiations: you concede a point, a set, an election — naming the moment you grant the other side a piece of the contest. Admit is the everyday cousin and covers your own faults. Among its unit-mates, acquiesce is silent going-along and accede grants a request; concede grants an argument.
